title: Defect-Free Grinding of Tungston Carbide at High Material Removal Rate
content: Grinding of tungsten carbide with cobalt binder (WC-Co) requires a high amount of energy input for a low material removal rate (MRR) resulting in a high tendency for surface damage. Further reducing WC-Co grind productivity is frequent stoppages of the process for dressing to remove cobalt (Co) binder adhering to the abrasive. This proof-of-concept sought to solve all these problems through laser assisted machining (LAM). Laser parameters in this work were selected to impart sufficient energy to melt Co binder without impacting the WC lattice. Subsequent grinding in the heat affected zone (HAZ) was done defect-free at 7.6 mm3/min/mm. Nonirradiated samples were damaged at a fraction of this MRR. This was possible because binder melting and re-solidification reduced yield strength and improved ductility under load. Grazing Incidence X-ray Diffraction (GIXRD) confirmed full recovery of the original WC-Co structure under the HAZ. This work has the potential to significantly improve productivity machining WC-Co through laser assisted near net shape rough grinding.
